AMR Responds To Drug Czar’s Opposing California Medical Marijuana "Regulation" Bill.
The Czar May Be Having Web Site Problems: His Press Release Is Not Online.

(Marijuananews note: The Democratic governor has angered his own AG and a majority of his party by opposing SB 848. Now he has been joined by the Drug Czar, which will be a political embarrassment.
See
California Governor Now Expected To Veto Vasconcellos’
Medical Marijuana Patient Registration Bill;
Committee Appropriates $1 Million For UC To Study Medical Marijuana.

This makes the political situation even more interesting. SB 848 is also opposed by Dennis Peron and Steve Kubby, who see it as an unnecessary capitulation to bad behavior by law enforcement.
See

Also,  in an odd twist, the Czar’s web site has not posted any press releases for July, including the one to which AMR is responding below. Maybe they are hungover from being entertained by the alcohol industry.
See

McCaffrey Fires New Salvo Against California Patients

SACRAMENTO, July 20 - Americans for Medical Rights, sponsors of California’s Prop. 215 in 1996 and other successful state ballot initiatives allowing the medical use of marijuana (Alaska, Washington State, Oregon and Nevada), See

"No one elected Gen. McCaffrey to run drug policy California, but he keeps trying to do it. Gen. McCaffrey has presided over America’s worst public policy failure since the war in Vietnam. He has no right to tell Californians how to create and enforce state laws, and he has no credibility when he tries.

"Gen. McCaffrey failed to convince the voters of California to defeat Prop. 215, he failed to convince voters in four other states to defeat similar initiatives, and he deserves to fail now in his effort to ride roughshod over elected officials to defeat responsible legislation.

"SB 848 would make enforcement of Prop. 215 more rational. It is a good bargain for police and patients alike. But Gen. McCaffrey seems to prefer the confusion and conflict that surround Prop. 215 today.

"The fact is, it’s too late for Gen. McCaffrey to try to erase the right to medical marijuana in California. What’s at stake with SB 848 is the rational and responsible implementation of that voter-approved law. Without it, we face a future with continued ambiguities and conflicts.

"Gen. McCaffrey’s statement today claims that SB 848 ‘ignores’ the recent National Academy of Sciences/Institute of Medicine (IOM) report on the medical use of marijuana.
See

"Were Gen. McCaffrey to support implementation of such a program, recommended in a report he commissioned, he might have some standing to oppose alternative programs that promise legal protection for medical marijuana patients. His failure to implement this compassionate alternative makes any policy recommendations from his office deeply suspect."
